Label the squares by their row and column, with the center square at \((3,3)\). The existing shaded squares are \((1,1)\), \((1,2)\), and \((2,3)\).

For the final design to have all 4 reflection axes of a square, every shaded square must be joined by all of its reflected images.

- \((1,1)\) is a corner. Its reflected images are the other 3 corners, so add \(3\) squares.
- \((1,2)\) lies one square in from a corner on the top edge. Its full symmetry orbit has \(8\) squares, and only \((1,2)\) is already shaded, so add \(7\) squares.
- \((2,3)\) lies directly above the center. Its full symmetry orbit has \(4\) squares (above, below, left, right of the center), and only \((2,3)\) is already shaded, so add \(3\) squares.

These orbits do not overlap, so the minimum number of additional shaded squares is
\[
3+7+3=13.
\]

\[
